+title: Adopt the Router-free FoundationModelsRanker seam
+---
+## What
+
+FoundationModelsRanker is removing its own Router dependency on branch `main`. Its public API changes in three ways that this package must follow:
+
+1. `SelectionConfig.model` changes from `@Sendable (String, Grammar) -> any AgentSession` to `@Sendable (String) -> any AgentSession`. The grammar argument is gone.
+2. `SelectionTier.idEnumGrammar(ids:) -> Grammar` becomes `SelectionTier.idEnumSchema(ids:) -> String`, which returns JSON Schema source text. Every schema rule stays: the per-element id `enum`, `uniqueItems`, and the `maxItems` cap.
+3. `RoutedEmbedderAdapter` and `RoutedAgentSession` are deleted. `TextEmbedding` and `AgentSession` stay public and unchanged.
+
+Ranker also adds `Searcher.init(_ items:, embedder:, session: any AgentSession, ...)`. The existing factory-form `init` keeps its signature, so `MetadataSearcher` does not have to change.
+
+**Do not start this task until the Ranker session reports that its manifest task has landed.** Ranker lands the seam change before the manifest change, so an early re-pin can catch a half-migrated API.
+
+Files to change:
+- `Package.resolved` — re-pin `FoundationModelsRanker` to the Router-free `main`. Run `swift package update FoundationModelsRanker`.
+- `Tests/FoundationModelsMetadataRegistryTests/TestSupport/SelectionFixtures.swift` — delete `import FoundationModelsRouter` (line 1). Change `makeSession(instructions:grammar:)` (line 112) to take instructions only. Change `receivedGrammarsBox`/`receivedGrammars` (lines 86, 102) from `[Grammar]` to `[String]`, or delete them if no test reads them.
+- `Tests/FoundationModelsMetadataRegistryTests/SelectionTests.swift`, `OverBudgetTests.swift`, `HotReloadTests.swift` — update every `SelectionConfig(model:)` call site to the one-argument closure. Update any assertion on grammar content to read the enum out of the schema string instead.
+- `Examples/ExamplesSupport/DemoAgentSession.swift` — update its `SelectionConfig` wiring to the one-argument closure.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+
+- [ ] No file in `Tests/` or `Examples/` imports `FoundationModelsRouter`.
+- [ ] No file names `Grammar`, `idEnumGrammar`, `RoutedEmbedderAdapter`, or `RoutedAgentSession`.
+- [ ] `Package.resolved` pins a FoundationModelsRanker revision whose manifest lists no dependencies.
+- [ ] `swift build` completes with no error.
+
+## Tests
+
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsMetadataRegistryTests/SelectionTests.swift` — every existing selection test passes against the one-argument seam, with no change in what it asserts about ranking.
+- [ ] Add a test that calls `SelectionTier.idEnumSchema(ids:)` with three ids and asserts the returned string contains all three ids in an `enum`, plus `uniqueItems` and a `maxItems` cap.
+- [ ] Run `swift test`. All tests pass.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass.
\ No newline at end of file

+**Do not start this task until the Ranker session reports that its manifest task (`^2q0p8gr`) has landed and is pushed.** Ranker lands the seam change before the manifest change, so an early re-pin catches a half-migrated API. As of the last report, Ranker task 1 of 9 is committed locally as `4b5c8bb`, nothing is pushed, and remote `main` still has the old API.
+
+### What `idEnumSchema(ids:)` returns
+
+It returns the WHOLE response schema, not the per-element enum. It starts from `Selection.generationSchema` (the `@Generable` type is `Selection { ids: [String] }`), makes three injections, and re-encodes:
+
+```json
+{
+  "type": "object",
+  "properties": {
+    "ids": {
+      "type": "array",
+      "items": { "type": "string", "enum": ["alpha", "bravo"] },
+      "uniqueItems": true,
+      "maxItems": 2
+    }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+The `enum` sits at `properties.ids.items.enum`. `uniqueItems` and `maxItems` sit one level up at `properties.ids`. `maxItems` equals `ids.count` exactly. An empty `ids` array gives an empty `enum` and `maxItems: 0`; that is intended.
+
+`maxItems` is load-bearing, not decoration. The xgrammar pipeline enforces `minItems`/`maxItems` but silently ignores `uniqueItems`. Without the cap, a compiled grammar permits an unbounded array of repeated enum members. Ranker observed a roughly 6150-token runaway on an off-topic intent. Keep the cap if this schema is ever compiled into a grammar.
